note: The place of the dive (cut/HANDOVER.md S1). oval: where the storm of the close view lies on the globe, in degrees on the globe's surface with the flow at rest as frozen for the dive. One place has one Sun, and the place is a storm the globe shows from orbit: the eye of the pale spiral oval east of the great red storm (its small tan eye lies at lon -3.19, lat -15.2 and measures 0.64 by 0.46 degrees), where the globe's own Sun stands 33 degrees over the ground while the camera is near (solved.sunElevationDeg), inside the 32 to 36 degrees at which the globe's light by its own curve (curve.json) is the light the close image was painted in. The great red storm itself stands under 48 degrees there, where that light is 1.6 to 2 times as strong. In the first named commit of round 2 the place lay at lon 3.42, lat 3.5 in a plain zone, and the painted storm stood on it as an island. Up to round 46 the place lay under a Sun of 57 degrees and the two lights were bridged by an exposure read from the camera's height; that bridge is gone. vortex: the centre of the close image's funnel in chart units (measured on the laid back image). The chart of the close view is laid on the globe so that the vortex sits on the oval and the baked Sun of the close image (deck.json light.azimuthDeg) points to the globe's Sun at the handover. freeze: the globe's band flow and the storm's swirl ease to rest from afterDiveStart seconds into the dive over easeSeconds. The spin eases from the hold's rate to rest over the dive by the shortest turn that does so without a turn back (a third of the turn at the hold's rate, solved.spinDeg is where it rests), stays there through the surface view and eases back to the hold's rate over the rise the same way, so the place is a rigid ground while it is near and the Sun moves over it by 1.5 degrees in the dive and 1.3 in the rise. solved is written by the tool: local is the frozen flow time in seconds, toSurface the rotation from the close view's frame to the globe's surface frame (the frame of the lookups, before the spin), n e u the chart's origin and axes there, twinHeight the close camera's height in radii. handover: the options of the engine's handover per kind and the law of the engine's one move (assets-src/shared/HANDOVER-NOTES.md). freeze.releaseAfterRise: seconds after the handover of the rise from which the frozen flow time is led back to the running one, reached at the end of the rise. solved.sun: the direction to the Sun at the handover on the chart's axes (x, y, up). solved.light: the globe's light on a ground that faces the Sun at that height, read from the globe's own curve; the plates hold the close image's light, so the plates over this number are the ground's albedo in the globe's coding, and the globe and the deck both draw them in the globe's light at every ground point (no exposure by height, no ratio between two programs).

handover.note: The change of view sits at the seams of the surface view (frames 3059 and 3240), so the whole dive and the whole rise are drawn by the globe's group, which holds the deck's own program (scene). No place picture, no sky frames, no limb reach: nothing of the change of view runs on the film's clock. The camera of both moves is the engine's one move (plan E; jupiter is off handover.ownPath in config/showcase.json): one glide from the hold, or to the pose after the rise, to the surface view's own seam pose carried at its velocity. pace, turn and liftPower are that move's law for this stop (StopPlan.eyeLaw): the bell of the height, the bell of the eye's direction and the power of the lift, found for the dive with npx tsx tools/law.ts --stop jupiter --kind dive, and for the rise with npx tsx assets-src/jupiter/deck/law.ts --kind rise --pop 1.06 --tries 3000 --seed 11, the same search held against the judge of npm run smooth itself at whole frames and at the capture rate and against a model of the stars' pop in the last frames of the move (the way of the sky on screen from one capture frame to the next over the median of its neighbours), so the rise ends without a jolt of the sky. Both are inside the limits of the path judge: the largest step of the dive is 0.062 and of the rise 0.076 of the mean a film frame (0.078 at the capture rate; 0.073 and 0.074 without the sidestep), against 0.08. The law of the rise was searched again for round 2 of the second note (the place moved to where the one Sun stands low): the size of the disc and the turn round the planet rise once and fall once, the phase runs one way from 58 to 94 degrees. pullBack (the engine's option for a rise that a travel follows, StopPlan.pullBack): the rise ends on its pose flying 3 radii a second above the drift along the line of the exit, picked up over its last 1.4 seconds, so the picture does not come to rest at the seam into the travel. The fastest point of the body's edge moves 6.55 px a film frame at its lowest (3317 + 1/2), 0.181 of the slower end of the judge's window, against the floor smooth.path.minLeave 0.07; without the option it read 0.36 px, 0.010. No from: with one the far end goes back while the leave is fastest and the size of the disc gets a second hill. 3.0 over 0.8 and 3.6 over 1.2 make the speed at the place climb again after its top (path judge red, 0.042 and 0.053 of the mean against 0.03); 3.0 over 1.4 leaves it one hill (0.000). The eye is nearer in every frame of the leave than without it and ends on the same pose: 3296 is drawn from 1.45 radii over the clouds. path.sidestep (the engine's option, Sidestep in src/director/handover.ts; mail 1021, ruling 2): the pose after the rise, which the one move glides toward, is turned round the place by 0.5 radii to the right and 0.75 up in its own frame, all of it for the first half of the rise's time, coming home with a smooth step over the last half (by 0.5), so the pose at the seam into the travel is the same to the bit. It is there for the level of the picture where the sky comes into the frame: the limb enters at the lower left corner (3283 + 1/2) and crosses the left edge over 6 capture frames (3284 to 3287; 3 without it), and the largest level step of the frames 3278 to 3300 is 0.74 at 3287 (1.36 at 3287 + 1/2 without it, limit 1.3). Chosen on a grid with the path judge: up 1 makes the turn's step red at 3243 (0.088 against 0.08, the glide turns toward the stepped pose from its first frame), right 1 and more makes the turn red at 3290 to 3295, on the way home; a negative up is red. The sidestep moves the heights between which no pixel is sky (scene.sky, scene.skyTurn: 0.14 to 0.3, were 0.14 to 0.41) and the frames 3315 to 3340 of the travel by a part of a pixel (the travel's carry reads the rise's last 1/300 s). skyFloor: see scene.sky.

limb.note: The globe's own rim. From orbit the lit edge is drawn a little inside the sphere with a warm glow of air beyond it (look.ts litEdge and edge): the far view's picture of the air over the limb, a soft edge one or two pixels wide. near: that rim is a presence by its size on screen and by nothing else. The measure is the glow's scale height (look.ts edge.air[1], in radii) over the foot of one pixel of the master frame at the limb point of the pixel's own ray (the distance along the ray to its point nearest the centre times the angle of a pixel, through the frame factor of src/core/frame.ts, so a capture at twice the size is the same picture): the inset of the lit edge and the cover of the glow are whole at and under the first number of pixels and gone at and over the second. Resolved over more pixels the glow would be the ground behind the horizon at a low cover, a mottled band tens of pixels wide, which the surface view does not have; there the air over the limb is the deck's own table (scene.limb). In the hold the measure is 1.22 pixels and in the judged frames 2997 and 3296 under 2.7, so they keep their bytes. Not a law of place, on purpose: in 129 frames of the approach and the retreat the limb passes within 261 units of the place, and a law of place would cut a notch into the rim there (assets-src/jupiter/deck/limbarc.ts prints both).

scene.note: One scene through the change of view (second review note, plan F). Nothing here is read from the film's clock. depth: the deck's own program (the deck's plates on the deck's own relief, lit by the globe's Sun through the deck's air) is drawn over the globe where its relief is deep enough to be seen. The relief lies between the two heights of look.shell in deck.json; its depth over the foot of one pixel of the master frame at the ground point (the distance along the ray times the angle of a pixel, through the frame factor of src/core/frame.ts, so a capture at twice the size is the same picture) is the measure: none of it at and under the first number of pixels, all of it at and over the second. A relief under the pixel's foot is a flat ground, and the globe draws that ground itself: the same plates laid back into its imagery by plates/upward.py with the tone the deck gives them. At the hold's lowest height (3.24 radii) the depth is 1.59 pixels at the point under the camera and less everywhere else, so the hold is the globe's alone and keeps its bytes; the measure is per pixel, so the far side of the place follows the near side as the camera comes down, and no number of it is a height (review of round 2, rulings of 22:40 and 23:34). limb: the deck's own horizon glow (the table of deck.json limb, measured on the approved close image) is the near view's picture of the air over the limb, and it stands over the deck's own ground, a law of place read per pixel: all of it where the horizon point of the pixel's ray (the ray's point nearest the globe's centre, laid on the sphere) lies within the first number of units, measured straight through the globe, from the far plate's centre on the sphere, none of it from the second number on (0.88 and 1.55 of the plate's half width: the inner edge of the plate's own join, and a point as far outside the plate as the plate's corner). It takes only what the globe's rim has given up by its size on screen (limb.near, the same measure on the same ray), so the air of one pixel is never drawn twice, and a far camera whose limb passes over the place draws none of it. The globe's shells are one mesh each with one gain a frame; they give way by the mean of the same product round the camera's true horizon circle, taken at as many directions as horizon says. In the film as flown it stands somewhere between frames 3017 and 3273 and everywhere between 3030 and 3263. The deck is on stage in the dive and the rise only, and that cuts nothing: outside them the two laws of this note give nothing in any frame (assets-src/jupiter/deck/limbarc.ts prints the frames; in the hold the limb lies 334 units and more from the place). air: not heights. The air of the approved view thins with the place on the ground: all of it where the ground point lies within the first share of the far plate's half width from the plate's centre, none beyond the second, the same from every height of the camera. sky: the share of the surface view's sky plate; the engine cuts the plate under the horizon it has at the seam (handover.dive.skyFloor, handover.rise.skyFloor), so its lower half never shows above the limb of a higher camera. skyTurn: the turn of the sky in the rise from this stop's own sky to the next stop's (the dive has no turn: the surface view takes no aim of its own, and its frame on the sphere is the globe view's, so from the hold to the surface the sky stands still and moves on screen only as the camera turns). All of it at and above the second height, none at and below the first. Both pairs of heights lie where no pixel of the frame is sky, so no frame shows two skies weighed against each other and no frame shows the sky turning by anything but the camera: with the pull back and the sidestep of the rise the sphere fills the frame from 0.0542 to 0.3246 radii on the way up (0.0430 to 0.4173 without the sidestep) and from 0.4429 to 0.0893 radii on the way down (assets-src/jupiter/sky/window.ts, --kind rise and --kind dive, to be run again when a path changes). Under those heights the sky is the place's own, over them the film's. halo: the glow of the globe's shells beyond the limb keeps the angle on screen it has at this height. At and above it the shells are drawn as the hold draws them; below it their scale heights shrink by the distance from the camera to the limb over that distance at this height, and their depth by the square root of the same, which keeps the level at the limb. Without it the widest shell, a tenth of a radius high, spread over the sky as a veil once the camera was near or inside it (frames 3279 to 3286 of the rise). The height lies under the hold's lowest height, so the hold keeps its bytes.
